issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s failure to comply with a rent-payment order does not require the Controller to strike out the tenant’s defence, and the Controller may extend the payment time or condone the default after considering the circumstances of the case.
material_facts: The landlord sought eviction for rent default, and the tenant admitted that rent was due.
The Controller ordered the tenant to pay or deposit the arrears within one month and to make subsequent monthly payments.
The tenant paid part of the amount but did not deposit the remaining arrears within the time ordered.

On remand, the Controller found that there had been a compromise between the parties and that the delay in depositing the remaining arrears was not wilful, deliberate, or contumacious; the Controller condoned the delay and allowed the tenant the benefit of the statutory protection against eviction.
The Tribunal and High Court upheld that decision, and the Supreme Court dismissed the landlord’s appeal.
issues.conclusion: The Controller’s power to strike out a tenant’s defence is discretionary, not mandatory. The Controller may extend the time for payment or deposit or condone default, but must decide whether to strike out the defence by applying its mind to the circumstances of the case rather than acting mechanically.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 14(1)(a), 14(2), 15(1), and 15(7) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958 provide the relevant framework. The word “may” in Section 15(7) makes striking out the defence discretionary. The discretion not to strike out the defence carries, by necessary implication, discretion to condone default or extend time. The Court applied Shyamcharan Sharma v. Dharamdas, which construed materially similar provisions of the Madhya Pradesh Accommodation Control Act; followed Ram Murti v. Bhola Nath on the operation of Section 15(7); and relied on Santosh Mehta v. Om Prakash for the discretionary, non-mandatory character of striking out the defence. Hem Chand v. Delhi Cloth & General Mills Co. Ltd. does not make eviction automatic upon non-compliance: although the Controller cannot treat the payment deadline as automatically extended, the question remains whether to strike out the defence under Section 15(7).

predicates.rent_default_eviction_proceeding: A landlord sought recovery of possession on the ground that the tenant had not paid rent.
predicates.tenant_failed_ordered_rent_payment: The tenant did not make the rent payment or deposit by the deadline set by the Controller.
predicates.controller_assessed_individual_circumsta: The Controller considered the circumstances surrounding the tenant’s non-payment when deciding what action to take.

issues.definition: When a landlord seeks eviction for rent default, the tenant misses a payment ordered by the Controller, and the Controller considers the individual circumstances, the Controller may decide whether to strike out the defence and may extend the payment time.
